text.p: Shares in Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem, which has been among the top gainers in a rallying Budapest bourse recently, have come down from their peaks, traders said on Wednesday.
They said Borsodchem fell as it followed prices on the SEAQ, where trading in Borsodchem's Global Depositary Receipts started at lower prices than in Budapest.

In Budapest Borsodchem shares opened at 6,420 forints, below Tuesday's close of 6,375 forints. At 1134 GMT its price stood at 6,095. On the SEAQ Borsodchem opened at $36.75 and at 1117 GMT was marked $1.15 down at $35.825. @
"In Budapest Borsodchem opened well above its prices on the SEAQ and then fell as the gap narrowed between the two markets," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities.
"Later the market saw strong selling pressure in Borsodchem from foreigners and now its price is falling on SEAQ, too, in profit-taking," Nagy said.
Elsewhere on the market most stocks continue their rally.
